note: MovieClip.setMask AS2 thunk, function start, size 0x87; 2013 counterpart 0x9ebb00 (VA 0xdebb00), bodies byte-identical. Pinned a second way: the entry sits in the MovieClip prototype method table in .rdata at 2012 0xdb3660, an array of {const char* name, handler} pairs whose name string reads "setMask", so the vtables.csv/match_2012_2013.csv path was not used at all. Semantics: result set to undefined before anything else and never changed; 0 args leaves the mask alone; null, undefined, a plain object, a TextField and a dead handle all CLEAR the mask rather than being refused; a live MovieClip argument reaches GFxSprite::SetMask. Ported as MCSetMask in GFxAS2Lib.cpp

GFxSprite::SetMask, size 0x123; 2013 0x9eb400. Retail keeps ONE pointer at GFxSprite+0x1CC for two roles, discriminated by GFxASCharacter+0xA0 bit 0x8000 (IsUsedAsMask): "my mask" when clear, "the sprite I am a mask for" when set, so a clip is either masked or a mask and never both, and most of the body is unlinking whichever role conflicts, recursively. Strong reference down (AddRef on store, Release on replace), weak back-pointer up. Setting a mask also zeroes the owner's SWF ClipDepth. The only invalidation is pMovieRoot->Flags |= 0x400, the optimized-advance-list dirty bit; there is no render-side invalidation. Ported as GFxCharacter::SetMask with a pointer per role and the exclusion spelled out
GFxSprite::SetMaskOwner, 2013 0x9ea2f0. Clears the new mask's own mask first, stores the owner and sets/clears the UsedAsMask bit. Folded into GFxCharacter::SetMask's second half
GFxSprite::GetMask, 2013 0x9ea2c0: null when the slot is empty or when this sprite is itself a mask. GetMask()/GetMaskOwner() with a pointer each
GFxASCharacter::IsUsedAsMask, 2013 0x9cb560, virtual at vtable+180, `(Flags >> 15) & 1`. Not ported as a function: with a pointer per role the predicate is `pMaskOwner != 0`

GFxDisplayContext::PreDrawMask, 2013 0xa53120. Sets the mask up with ITS OWN parent's world matrix (mask->pParent at +0x20), not the masked clip's - the one fact that makes a scripted mask different from a ClipDepth mask. Ported as the ctx.StageMatrix * GFxCharacterWorldMatrix(mask->GetParent()) composition in GFxDisplayPushScriptedMask

GFxDisplayContext::PushAndDrawMask, 2013 0xa53340: BeginSubmitMask(MaskStackCount ? Increment : Clear), push the mask onto a 64-entry stack, ++DrawingMaskDepth, PushBlendMode, mask->Display, PopBlendMode, --DrawingMaskDepth, EndSubmitMask. Ported without the blend-mode pair (this tree has no per-character blend mode) and with a counter instead of the stack
GFxDisplayContext::PopMask, 2013 0xa533d0: DisableMask only when the last mask comes off. Ported as the bMaskPushed arm at the tail of GFxSprite::Display

GFxSprite::Display, size 0x2b2, 2013 0x9f1780. Two things taken from it this package: the head early-out is `if ((Flags & 3) != 1 && (Flags & 0x8000) == 0) return`, i.e. invisible AND not serving as a mask - so a mask IS drawn while invisible and, note, a VISIBLE mask is still drawn as ordinary content too (GFx does not hide a mask; the content has to); and the self-healing arm that calls SetMask(0) when the mask is no longer this clip's mask. The scripted mask is pushed around the whole sprite, self and children, and popped after PostDisplay

GFxSprite::PointTestLocal, size 0x36a, 2013 0x9f2320. The scripted mask IS honoured in hit testing: pt_mask = inverse(mask world) * this world * pt, then mask->PointTestLocal(pt_mask, flags), and a miss ends the test. Ported verbatim with GMatrix2D::SetInverse + Prepend, which is retail's own expression

GFxSprite::GetTopMostMouseEntity does NOT reference the mask slot; it reaches scripted masks only through each child's PointTestLocal. Left alone deliberately - adding a mask test here would be an invention

MovieClip.attachMovie, function start, size 0x317, 2013 0x9f63b0. The +0x4000 is `add eax, 4000h` at 0x9ffb3e, applied to (int)ToNumber(arg2) BEFORE the GFxCharPosInfo constructor; the validity test at 0x9ffb55 is on the already-biased value and UNSIGNED, `> 0x7EFFFFFD`, with the error naming the biased number. Both ported into MCAttachMovie

MovieClip.duplicateMovieClip, size 0x105, 2013 0x9eb9f0. CloneDisplayObject(this, name, depth + 0x4000, initObj) with the bias inline at the call site and NO range check and NO warning, unlike attachMovie. Ported as MCDuplicateMovieClip + GFxSprite::CloneDisplayObject. MEASURED UNUSED: the cook never calls duplicateMovieClip and never emits the cloneSprite opcode

GFxASCharacter::CharacterGetDepth, size 0x39, 2013 0x9c4700. `add edi, 0FFFFC000h` then stored as INTNUMBER: internal - 0x4000, NO clamp, so a timeline clip answers a negative AS depth - internal 1 reads -16383, matching agent FB's live capture of mainMenu_mc exactly. Ported as MCGetDepth. MEASURED UNUSED by this cook

MovieClip.getNextHighestDepth, size 0x64, 2013 0x9ebcf0. `sub eax, 3FFFh; sets cl; dec ecx; and ecx, eax` = max(0, largest - 0x3FFF). The constant is 0x3FFF, not 0x4000. GetLargestDepthInUse answers -1 on an empty list, so the result is 0 there. Ported as MCGetNextHighestDepth. 130 call sites in the cook - the most-called depth method by far

MovieClip.removeMovieClip, size 0x7c, 2013 0x9ed360. SIGNED `this->Depth >= 0x4000`, no upper bound; the else arm logs "%s.removeMovieClip() failed - depth must be >= 0" with the handle's SHORT name (+0x08), where attachMovie's message uses the full path (+0x0C). The parent is not checked here. unloadMovie does NOT share this handler - it is 0x9f3e50 and goes to the load queue. Ported as MCRemoveMovieClip; agent EZ's bScriptCreated flag is deleted, the depth is the test again

GFxCharacterHandle::ResolveCharacter, size 0x17, 2013 0x9c4600, bodies identical. `pCharacter ? pCharacter : GFxMovieRoot::FindTarget(root, this->NamePath)`. No caching of either answer. Was a stub returning its argument; now real
GFxCharacterHandle::ForceResolveCharacter, 2013 0x9c4610: the same lookup unconditionally. Nothing in this tree calls it; not ported

GFxCharacterHandle's constructor. Interns NamePath as parent->GetAbsolutePath() + '.' + Name at construction - re-resolution is by ABSOLUTE path from the movie root, not relative to the original parent. Ported into GFxASCharacter::CreateCharacterHandle
GFxCharacterHandle::ChangeName rewrites Name and NamePath together. Ported into GFxASCharacter::SetName
GFxMovieRoot::FindTarget, 2013 0x9f7ee0: null when there is no _level0 or the path is empty, otherwise _level0's own AS environment resolves it. Ported inline in ResolveCharacter

MovieClip.startDrag, size 0x1d2, 2013 0x9f0270. lockCenter defaults false; the bounds arm needs all five arguments, multiplies by 20 into twips and normalises left/right and top/bottom. Ported as MCStartDrag. MEASURED UNUSED: _common.P_Slider::StartDrag drives its own onEnterFrame off _parent._xmouse and never calls startDrag

MovieClip.stopDrag, size 0x4b, 2013 0x9f0450. It clears exactly ONE field, DragState.pCharacter at GFxMovieRoot+0x23D4, and leaves the lock flag, the bounds and the centre delta stale - harmless because DoMouseDrag gates on `this == DragState.pCharacter`. GFxASCharacter::DoMouseDrag, 2013 0x9c6250. Gate on identity, pointer into the parent's space, add the centre delta, clamp to the bounds, SetAcceptAnimMoves(false), then _x and _y in pixels. Ported; called once per GFxMovieRoot::Advance instead of through the optimized play list

GFxMovieRoot::GetDragState, with SetDragState 2012 0x9e1260 / 2013 0x9d7920: the 0x20-byte struct is copied whole. Ported as a reference accessor; the struct's nine fields are reproduced at their retail meanings
